mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby lowering S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 30-day period of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment costs measured by PAYEMS accelerates wage growth, which compresses real disposable income and dampens equity demand, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative correlation with PAYEMS wage growth (Pearson IC > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a shift from supply-side to demand-side constraints, pushing equity valuations higher and driving positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 2% while INDPRO decreases by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically different from a baseline of balanced demand-supply (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which raises uncertainty and elevates risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO in a downward trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly lower than during the prior 3-month expansion period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals policy tightening and reduced household spending, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the prior 10-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly pay growth (PAYEMS) outpaces inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points, real wages expand, boosting equity demand and producing positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no significant correlation with the (PAYEMS - CPIAUCSL) signal (Pearson IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in retail sales proxies (not available in the given catalog) would indicate consumer confidence, but since we cannot use retail sales, instead a sharp increase in HOUST alongside a decline in RSAFS suggests shifting demand structure favoring equities and drives positive 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% while RSAFS decreases by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than during periods of balanced demand indicators (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where both FEDFUNDS is above 3% and UNRATE is below 4%, the combination of high policy rates and low unemployment typically precedes a risk-off environment that produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative during the defined regime (IC > -0.05).
